notes: The Arduino Nano 33 BLE is not in the catalogue, so it is a new part type with only the ports used (A4=SDA, A5=SCL, GND, 3V3, VIN). The diagram's '3V' pin is named 3V3.

The diagram shows the two pull-up resistors and wires joined directly with no breadboard. The hardware list names 2 mini breadboards. I used one breadboard (bb1) as the junction for the shared SCL and SDA lines and the 3V3 rail. Columns 5 and 7 and rail tp are my own choice.
The reader's 3V pin feeds both pull-up resistors (red line). The writer's 3V pin is not connected.
Teal = A5 (SCL), yellow = A4 (SDA), brown = GND. The diagram shows a wire crossing without a junction where the yellow SDA line passes over the teal SCL line. They are not connected there.
Both boards are powered and connected to the computer by USB. The usb-cable has no catalogue ports, so those edges use null ports. The computer is not modelled.
The manual lists 10 jumper wires, but only 6 are needed for this circuit. Resistor values are written as 4700 (4.7 kΩ).
